newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurocourt rules on "idiot" Austrian politician.
newsitem.headline: Eurocourt rules on "idiot" Austrian politician.

text.p: The European Court of Human Rights ruled on Tuesday that an Austrian journalist was wrongly fined for calling far-right politician Joerg Haider an idiot after he said all World War Two soldiers fought for peace.

"It is true that calling a politician a Trottel (idiot) in public might offend him. However the word appeared proportionate to the indignation knowingly aroused by Mr Haider," the Strasbourg-based court said in its ruling.

Gerhard Oberschlick, editor of the weekly Forum, described Haider as a "Trottel" in a 1991 article on a speech in which Haider said that all World War Two soldiers fought for peace and freedom whatever side they were on.
Haider also said that all World War Two soldiers had helped found modern democracy, and that only those who risked their lives in the war had a right to free speech.
"Mr Haider had clearly intended to be provocative and consequently to arouse strong reactions," the court said.

Haider sued Oberschlick who was fined 4,000 Austrian schillings ($326) in 1991 for insulting him. The Vienna appeals court upheld the conviction the following year but cut the fine to 1,000 schillings.
The European court said Oberschlick should get his money back and awarded him 150,000 schillings for costs and expenses.
